alternatives.root_cause: A bad deploy of checkout put a broken or wrong-version artifact into service.
alternatives.why_not: Plausible and nearly indistinguishable from bad_config at this resolution, but a crash-looping artifact usually produces connection failures at the proxy with checkout emitting nothing; a uniformly-erroring-but-responding checkout fits a wrong value more than a wrong binary.

alternatives.root_cause: payment or another checkout dependency became slow, and checkout failed waiting on it.
alternatives.why_not: No downstream service alerted, and a latency cascade would normally trip the dependency's own alert and appear as timeouts rather than an instantaneous high error rate at exactly the same second across all callers.

verdict.summary: checkout is failing on every request because of a wrong configuration value (most likely a bad endpoint/address or credential for one of its downstream dependencies, e.g. the Kafka broker or a gRPC target), so it returns errors that surface at frontend, frontend-proxy and the load-generator.
verdict.reasoning: The alerting set is checkout plus its entire caller chain (frontend -> frontend-proxy -> load-generator), which is exactly the shape of errors propagating upward from a single broken node. None of checkout's own dependencies (product-catalog, currency, cart, email, payment, shipping) alert, and product-catalog/cart are shared with frontend yet show nothing, so the break is in checkout itself rather than beneath it. The simultaneous onset across all four services and a high error rate (rather than latency or timeouts) points to fast, deterministic failures - requests rejected immediately, not waited on - which fits a wrong configured address/port/credential or a dependency checkout talks to that is off the graph (Kafka is noted absent and checkout is its producer). checkout is not a flagd consumer in this catalog, which argues against a flag flip; a resource or disk problem would normally ramp rather than start cleanly at one instant.
open_questions: checkout's own error logs: connection refused / unknown host / auth rejected vs. deadline exceeded vs. panic on startup
whether checkout pods restarted or rolled at 09:29 and what image/config version they came up with
whether checkout's Kafka producer is erroring (Kafka is absent from the graph but checkout depends on it in this topology)
checkout request latency distribution - fast failures (config) vs. timeouts (dependency latency)
error rates and saturation on payment, cart and shipping to confirm they are genuinely healthy
